messages.author: 9a25c34b3581b87f
messages.subject: rsf.fit() problem with categorical data
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am currently working on rsf.fit() using a combination of both categorical and numeric data. However, I keep encountering the following error:
Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) : error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'is.factor': cannot allocate vector of size 16.2 Mb

Initially, I suspected that the issue might be related to the sizes of my rasters. I tried to crop everything based on my individual's AKDE (+500 m as a buffer), but this did not resolve the problem. 
I've previously used all of my rasters in long/lat coordinates and it worked fine. However, I encountered some errors when plotting suitability maps with long/lat rasters (Error in CTMM$COV[TERMS, TERMS, drop = FALSE] : subscript out of bounds). This is why I am now reworking my analysis using projected raster layers (in UTM 51N). One note is that I received a warning message that stated In .local(x, ...) :
  This function is only useful for Raster* objects with a longitude/latitude coordinates.

The code I've been using is as follows:
ctmm:::rsf.fit(bear_acorn[[i]], UD = AAKDE[[i]],
               R = list(elevation = crop(env_all_51n[[1]], bb01_ext + 500),
                      ndvi = acorn_ndvi_stack[[which(names(acorn_ndvi_stack) == summary(bear_acorn[[i]])$identity)]],
                      tri = env_all_51n[[2]],
                      dtr = env_all_51n[[3]],
                      dtw = env_all_51n[[4]],
                      dtt = env_all_51n[[5]],
                      dty = env_all_51n[[6]]),
               forest = as.factor(env_all_51n[[7]])),
               debias = TRUE, error = 0.01, integrator = "Riemann", interpolate = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)

Any insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!

Thank you very much,

Fang

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: rsf.fit() problem with categorical data
parts:
Hi Fang,

I suspect you need to specify raster::as.factor(env_all_51n[[7]])). If that doesn't work, you can send me a minimal working example (data + script), then I can take a look at it.
Same with Error in CTMM$COV[TERMS, TERMS, drop = FALSE]. If you can provide me with a minimal working example, then I would like to fix that.

The raster warning is from raster::area() and shouldn't matter unless you choose a bad projection.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: rsf.fit() problem with categorical data
parts:
Hi Fang,

raster::unique(forest) returns 423,623 floating point values, so as.factor is making this a categorical variable with 423,623 categories, which causes a huge slowdown. Maybe you want to use round() first? The data do appear to be clustered around 0,1,2,3. raster::round() doesn't appear to be exported, so you will need to explicitly load the raster library to round the values.

Best,
Chris
